1968 protest discipline timeline

 

Number of Disciplinary Actions

Diplomas Withheld

Suspensions

50

100

150

200

250

300

350

400

Four students are suspended for not attending disciplinary meetings.

May 3rd, 1968

The New York Police Department arrests over 130 students in Hamilton Hall for protesting the suspensions. Those students are set for suspensions.

The dean of Columbia College threatens to withhold diplomas to incentivise graduating seniors to plead guilty for protest participation.

June 3rd, 1968

15 diplomas are ultimately withheld from seniors.

21 students of over 130

are still suspended.

September 18th, 1968

The Manhattan district attorney’s office drops most trespassing charges against arrested students.

October 15th, 1968

The University rescinds all disciplinary sentences against the spring protestors. Suspended students are allowed to reapply to the University.

Febuary 6th, 1968

Source: Columbia University Libraries

Note: Data for bar charts is reflected within the text for the timelines. Any actions taken by the University intended to reprimand or punish students for protest activity were considered “disciplinary actions.”

Graphic by Emily Ta
